title: Elevated work platforms and competence
audience: Owners, supervisors and quoting staff on the window cleaning (all heights) track who may be asked to use or price an elevated work platform. Not a platform operator course.
learningOutcomes: Identify which platform types require a high risk work licence in the states where the licence matrix confirms the rule.
Check operator competence, platform condition and the rescue plan before an elevated platform is used.
Price elevated platform work only on evidence of licensed operation, equipment and authority.

instruction.heading: What an elevated work platform is
instruction.body: An elevated work platform lifts a worker and their tools to a working height. Platform types differ. A boom-type elevating work platform extends on an arm and has a platform at the end. A scissor lift raises a platform vertically. Each type has different stability, reach and control characteristics, so each needs its own check. The type of platform decides which licence rules apply, and the rules differ by state and territory.

instruction.heading: Licence rules from the official pages
instruction.body: In New South Wales and Queensland, a boom-type elevating work platform needs a WP high risk work licence where the boom is 11 metres or more, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. That threshold is stated on the national model code page (December 2025), the New South Wales page, the Tasmanian page (last updated 1 December 2023), the Western Australian page (updated 13 August 2026) and the Northern Territory bulletin (no date shown). Queensland excludes platforms shorter than 11 metres (no date shown). The Victorian WP page gives the class with no boom-length threshold (reviewed 30 June 2026). Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Scissor lifts need no licence in Victoria (reviewed 30 June 2026) or the Northern Territory (no date shown), and the national class list names no class for them (no date shown). The other pages checked do not address scissor lifts, so check the rule for your state before use, and do not assume a rule from another state.

instruction.heading: Operator competence and the licence question
instruction.body: Where a licence is required, only a licensed operator may run the platform. Check the licence class, its validity and that it covers the platform type before the platform moves. A licence held by one worker does not authorise the business to perform the work, and it does not cover the other workers on the job. Record who holds each licence, the class, and the regulator who issued it, and keep a copy of the record on the job. The national model code says a licence must be sighted and should be recorded at induction (December 2025).

instruction.heading: Pre-use checks and the rescue plan
instruction.body: Before use, check the platform's condition, the manufacturer's inspection record, the outriggers or stabilisers, the ground, the controls, the emergency lowering method and the guardrail or restraint system as applicable. Confirm that the platform will not be overloaded and that the wind and weather are inside the plan. Prepare a rescue plan that says how a trapped or unwell operator is lowered or brought down, who does it, and how quickly. The plan must exist before the platform is raised.

instruction.heading: Exclusion zones and public protection
instruction.body: The area beneath and around the platform is a drop zone. Tools and cleaning equipment must be tethered or held, and the zone must be kept clear of people and property using barriers or a supervisor. A platform that cannot keep the zone clear is not suitable for the site.

instruction.heading: Honest pricing for platform work
instruction.body: Platform work can be priced higher than ground-based work because it needs equipment, a licensed operator and planning. That price is supportable only when the licence, the equipment, the operator and the authority are verified, and the platform type is confirmed. Do not quote an elevated platform rate on the basis of a worker's general experience. Put the platform hire or ownership cost, the operator cost and the exclusions in writing, and tie the rate to the verified evidence.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, operator competence or authority to operate any elevated work platform. Boom-type platform licences apply at a boom length of 11 metres or more, as set out above. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start.

procedure: Identify the platform type and confirm which state or territory rule applies to it.
Check that the licensed operator holds a current licence class that covers the platform type.
Inspect the platform, its controls, stabilisers, ground and emergency lowering method before use.
Write the rescue plan, name who carries it out and confirm they are able to do so.
Set the drop zone, barriers and tool tethering, and assign a supervisor to hold the zone.
Confirm the wind and weather are inside the plan, and stop if they change.
Record the licence details, the inspection, the rescue plan and the zone controls.

workedExamples.situation: A business plans to use a hired boom-type platform to clean the upper windows of a shop front in New South Wales.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be confirmed before the platform is raised?
workedExamples.reasoning: The NSW page (dated 15 June 2026) says a WP licence is needed where the boom is 11 metres or more. Check the operator's licence class and validity, confirm it covers the platform, and record the details. Set a drop zone on the footpath with barriers and a supervisor. Write the rescue plan and check the wind. Do not raise the platform until all of these are recorded.

workedExamples.situation: A worker plans to use a scissor lift in Victoria without a licence and says the lift is small.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the scissor lift need a licence, and what else must be checked?
workedExamples.reasoning: The WorkSafe Victoria licence page (reviewed 30 June 2026) says scissor lifts do not need a WP licence. The worker must still check the platform, the ground, the drop zone, the emergency lowering method and the authority from the site controller. The absence of a licence does not remove the need for a competence check and a rescue plan.

equipmentAndPpe: Platform inspection record and manufacturer instructions
Operator licence record with class, validity and issuing regulator
Rescue plan written before the platform is raised
Barriers, cones, tool tethers and a supervisor for the drop zone
Fall-restraint or guardrail system as the platform design requires, and eye protection and footwear

commonErrors.error: Assuming a scissor lift needs the same licence as a boom platform in every state.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state rule for each platform type. The official pages checked confirm the scissor-lift position only for Victoria and the Northern Territory.

commonErrors.error: Relying on a licence held by a different worker.
commonErrors.prevention: Check that the operator holds the licence for the platform type and that it is current.

commonErrors.error: Raising the platform without a written rescue plan.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the rescue plan and confirm the named person can carry it out before the platform moves.

commonErrors.error: Quoting an elevated rate without evidence of licence, equipment and authority.
commonErrors.prevention: Tie the rate to verified evidence and state the exclusions in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Boom-type elevating work platform: a WP licence applies where the boom is 11 metres or more in New South Wales, and a shorter boom may not need it there. Queensland's page excludes platforms shorter than 11 metres (no date shown), and Victoria's WP class page gives no boom length (reviewed 30 June 2026).

Scissor lifts: no high risk work licence is needed in Victoria (reviewed 30 June 2026) or the Northern Territory (no date shown). Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start.

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, operator competence or authority to operate a platform. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start.

qualityStandard: The platform type is identified and the applicable state rule is recorded.
The operator licence class and validity are checked and recorded before use.
A written rescue plan exists before the platform is raised.
The drop zone is controlled and recorded, and the quote reflects only verified evidence.
documentationEvidence: Platform type, state rule applied and the decision on licence need
Operator licence details with class, validity and issuing regulator
Platform inspection record and rescue plan
Drop zone record and quote with exclusions
summary: Platform type decides the licence rule, and the rule differs by state.

Official pages checked put boom-type platform licences at 11 metres or more in New South Wales, place platforms shorter than 11 metres outside the Queensland definition, and give the WP class without a boom length in Victoria.
Check the operator, the platform, the rescue plan and the drop zone before use.
Price platform work only on verified licence, equipment and authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which platform type needs a high risk work licence to operate in Victoria, according to the WorkSafe Victoria licence page?
options: A scissor lift on the job site
A stepladder on the job site
A water-fed pole on the job site
A boom-type elevating work platform

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the Queensland licence rule exclude from the boom-type platform definition?
options: Platforms shorter than 11 metres
Platforms over 20 metres
Platforms used indoors
Platforms with a rescue plan

knowledgeChecks.question: Before an elevated platform is raised, what must exist?
options: A customer signature only, with the date and time
A written rescue plan and a checked licence for the operator
A discount for the customer on the job today and the week
A ladder on site for the crew to use at the base today

knowledgeChecks.question: A licence held by one worker is relied on for the whole crew. What is wrong with this?
options: Nothing, one licence covers the whole crew on the site, the business and the platform
The crew needs only the business licence for the platform on the whole site
A licence covers the licensed operator and the platform type, not the crew or the business
The customer must hold the licence for the platform, the site and the job

knowledgeChecks.question: Is an elevated platform rate supportable on general worker experience alone?
options: Yes, experience is enough for the platform work
Yes, if the platform is hired for the whole job
Yes, if the customer agrees to the platform use
No, it needs licence, equipment and authority evidence
